properties.name: Adam's Dwelling (930 years)
properties.description: Adam lived 930 years outside the Garden. The pre-Flood world had conditions allowing extreme longevity.
properties.debate: Pre-Flood longevity may relate to genetic vitality, atmospheric conditions, or other factors altered by the Flood.

properties.name: Enoch's Walk with God
properties.popup: Enoch walked with God and was taken - Genesis 5:21-24
properties.description: Enoch lived 365 years then 'was not, for God took him.' He did not experience death.
properties.debate: Enoch's translation demonstrates God's power over death and foreshadows the resurrection.

properties.name: Methuselah's Region (969 years)
properties.description: Methuselah lived 969 years, the longest recorded lifespan. His name may mean 'when he dies, it shall come' - he died the year of the Flood.
properties.archaeology: Ancient king lists from Sumer also record extraordinarily long pre-Flood reigns, preserving memory of antediluvian longevity.

properties.name: Lamech (Seth's line)
properties.popup: Noah's father, man of faith - Genesis 5:28-31
properties.description: Lamech named his son Noah ('rest'), prophesying relief from the curse on the ground.

properties.name: Noah's Birthplace
properties.popup: Righteous man in corrupt generation - Genesis 5:28-32
properties.description: Noah was born when his father Lamech was 182. He would become the preacher of righteousness who built the ark.
properties.debate: Noah lived somewhere in the pre-Flood world, which was destroyed. Post-Flood geography differs significantly.
